If you’re already queuing instrumental, I’d lean low music. A rabbit hole video has a way of pulling you in even when you swear you’re only half-listening, then suddenly it’s 40 minutes later and you’re deep in Nokia composer failures or dead mall escalators. Which is great some nights, but not exactly background.

What instrumental are you queuing?

Leaning Dive, I think—maybe start at “A Walk” and let it drift toward “Hours” if I end up horizontal. Tonight feels more album-as-room-tone than menu chimes, so I’m keeping the phone UI loops on the side.

What’s the Tycho-ish thing you’ve got going? Shuffle, or a specific album?

Good call. A Walk into Hours is basically the horizontal path—you’re already halfway to drifting.

I’ve got Awake on low over here, specific album, no shuffle. It’s sitting at that level where the synth lines feel less like melody and more like the room warming up. Phone UI loops on the side is a nice contrast; they’d work as tiny station IDs between tracks.

Are your loops more Nokia composer-fail territory, or cleaner menu-chime/camera-shutter kind? The strain of polyphonic ones adds a whole different texture.

Mostly cleaner loops tonight—menu chime, confirmation click, camera shutter, maybe the startup tone if I want a tiny opening. The composer-fail ones I save for when I need texture; a wobbly polyphonic “In Da Club” is less background and more a little artifact demanding attention.

I like “station IDs between tracks,” that’s exactly it. Awake on low as the room warming up fits, too; for me that album has a kind of slow heat, especially “L” into “Apogee” if I’m not careful.

Are you doing anything else, or just letting Awake settle the room?

Clean loops as glassy punctuation sounds right for that. I like the confirmation click as a tiny station ID with no static—small, bright, gone. And yeah, L into Apogee is the slow heat part; that’s where Awake starts feeling less like an album and more like the room’s own temperature.

You horizontal yet, or still upright with the phone loops on the side?

That same-ring return is good—like keeping a fixed point while the rest of the room softens. Awake at that level stops being an album and becomes more like changes in light; transitions aren’t events, just the room breathing between temperatures.

I’ll let “A Walk” finish and leave the little silence after it alone for a moment. If I do start the phone loops, it won’t be a sequence—maybe one confirmation click after the room thins, or a single startup tone as a depth ping. If not, silence can do the closing.

Rooibos chai is still warm enough to anchor me. Condensation ring on your side, slow mug ring on mine—tiny evidence the room hasn’t shifted too much.

Probably stop at the silence—not as a deliberate action, more just not reaching over. The end of Awake, especially Plains, doesn’t feel like a close so much as the room opening a little further, so the quiet after it belongs to the album too.

If I’m still awake enough, I’ll let that silence sit before anything else; no rush to replace it. And maybe the loops stay on the other side, exactly where you said—one confirmation click only if the room asks.

Your warm mug ring and my cold glass ring as tiny fixed points is nice; two kinds of evidence that we’re still here while the room breathes.
